title: Module 6 · Lesson 3 — Data quality, freshness and access control

lines: A RAG system that was accurate at launch decays silently.
Freshness, permissions, and provenance are ongoing engineering, not setup steps.

say.0: A rag system that was accurate at launch decays silently.

lines: Picture an airline assistant that answers cabin crew questions from manuals and safety bulletins.
At launch, every answer checks out.
Six months later, it still quotes a retracted safety bulletin.
The bulletin was deleted at the source, but its chunks never left the index.
Nightly full rebuilds don't scale, and leave long windows of stale answers.
Instead, catch changes with webhooks or change-data-capture, and upsert each document by a stable ID.

say.1: Instead, catch changes with webhooks or change-data-capture, and up-sert each document by a stable I D.

lines: Deletions are tombstoned, so removed content stops being retrievable immediately.
Every chunk also carries a version and timestamp, so answers prefer the current revision.
Incident reports are for the safety team only, so every chunk gets access metadata at ingestion.
The vector search is then limited to what this user may see.
Filtering after retrieval leaks what exists, through rankings and result counts.
Where isolation must be absolute, use separate collections or namespaces per tenant.
Permissions also change: a purser who left the safety team last week shouldn't still see its reports.
So check access at query time, against current permissions, not ones baked into the index.
The corpus contradicts itself too: an old rule and its replacement, a regional variant and a global default.
Metadata like effective date, status, and authority lets ranking prefer the authoritative one.
The model should surface conflicts rather than silently pick one.
For example: the current rule from June says this, but the superseded one said that.
Incident reports also hold passenger names and phone numbers.
Redact or tokenise them at ingestion, because anything embedded is effectively distributed.
NeMo Curator detects and redacts personal data at scale.
And if data can't leave your trust boundary, redact at the boundary or self-host with NIM.

say.0: Nemo Curator detects and redacts personal data at scale.

lines: Classic exam trap: a retracted policy keeps getting cited because the deletion never reached the index.
The fix is deletion propagation, and the lesson below shows how.
